body_markdown:
> I don’t get no respect.
>
>
> *—Rodney Dangerfield, comedian, 1969*


Yes, of course: When you think of premium smaller SUVs, the first two typically mentioned are the Honda CR-V and Toyota RAV4, not the Nissan Rogue. After all, the CR-V and RAV4 have been around for about 30 years now, sold under the same name, which helps continuity. And both have been, and remain, good products.


But perhaps it’s time to show a little respect for the Rogue, which has been Nissan’s CR-V and RAV4-fighter since 2007. As it approaches its 20th birthday, Nissan is introducing the fourth generation of its trucklet as the “all-new” 2027 model. Yes, it’s been redesigned inside and out with some edgier, rather handsome styling, courtesy of a team that included designer Hiren Patel,[who we profiled](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/he-works-at-nissan-design-america-or-he-did-when-i-spoke-to-him/) a year ago. In this[YouTube video,](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mOwbLp6wxA8) he shows off their work on the Rogue.


Appropriately, it remains familiar—no real reason to mess with success too much, because the Rogue is Nissan’s best-selling vehicle.


Nissan


Indeed, in the second quarter of this year, Rogue sales were up almost 30 percent over the same quarter in 2025, with 69,796 Rogues leaving dealership lots, compared to 47,461 in the second quarter of 2025. And it has accomplished that without the hybrid system that has boosted RAV4 and CR-V sales.


Until now. Rogue may be a little late to the hybrid party, but it appears it’s arriving well-prepared to meet the competition. Called, as you’d figure, the Nissan Rogue Hybrid, it uses Nissan’s hybrid “e-POWER” technology that uses the gas-powered engine to charge a battery that powers dual electric motors. EPA ratings aren’t out yet, but Nissan’s own testing projects an in-city number of 40 mpg, with 36 mpg on the highway and 38 mpg combined.


Nissan


It goes on sale this fall, beginning with the all-wheel-drive SR model equipped with the Technology Package, starting at $41,490. Other hybrid-powered models will become available in early 2027; the starting price for the base-model SV hybrid will be $35,490. Shipping adds $1575. For now at least, all the U.S. Rogue Hybrids will be built in Japan.


Wait, wasn’t there a plug-in hybrid Rogue? Well, kind of. For 2026, Nissan did indeed introduce the plug-in Nissan Rogue Hybrid, but it was just a rebadged Mitsubishi Outlander, co-opted to attack the no-hybrid hole in the Rogue’s lineup until this e-POWER model was ready for ’27. Note that the Mitsubishi-built version started at $45,990, which is about $2000 more than the absolute top-of-the-line 2027 Rogue Hybrid Platinum AWD model will cost. There’s nothing wrong with the plug-in Rogue, and it appears there are some remaining on dealer lots that you could probably get a decent deal on. (Nissan has confirmed to other outlets that it is ending production of the Mitsu-Rogue now that its own is here.)


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


Nissan


So how does the 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid drive? We don’t know yet, but it’ll be different. The turbocharged 1.5-liter, three-cylinder gasoline engine is tuned to act as a generator to power the battery that, in turn, powers the front wheels with one electric motor, and the rear wheels with another. The gas engine is never connected to the wheels, and that means that there’s no transmission. Torque, which is the measure of pulling power, should come on quickly. According to Nissan, this e-POWER system “makes Rogue Hybrid smoother, quicker and quieter than competing hybrid SUVs.”


Nissan


Indeed, Nissan notes that the “Rogue Hybrid is the only hybrid in its class with a 100 percent electric drivetrain.” Even though, with the addition of the gas engine, this technically isn’t an electric vehicle. Still, Nissan may have to sell customers, who may push back at the idea of an EV, that the Rogue Hybrid, which *is* an EV but really *isn’t,* erases range anxiety. In addition to the mpg figures, A 504-mile range with the EPA-highway estimate ought to be a pretty convincing talking point.


But fear not, dedicated haters of EVs and hybrids: Nissan will continue to sell conventional combustion-powered Rogues in the 2027 model year. In fact, they’re already out: A nicely-equipped 2027 Nissan Rogue SV non-hybrid with front-wheel drive starts at $30,690, plus that $1575 destination fee. It’s powered by a carryover 1.5-liter turbocharged three-cylinder with 201 horsepower, rated at 28 mpg city, 33 highway, and 30 combined.
